explanation: Son of Solomon and king of Israel, who succeeded his father on the throne.
An alternative name for Rehoboam, used in various Bible translations.
A former servant under Solomon who became leader of the ten northern tribes and founded the rival kingdom of Israel.
One of Israel's twelve tribes and the name of the southern kingdom that emerged after the division of the kingdom, with Jerusalem as its capital.
The city where Jeroboam was proclaimed king over the ten northern tribes.
Members of the tribe of Levi, one of Israel's twelve tribes, who had special religious duties and roles in the temple.
The holy building in Jerusalem where the Israelites worshiped God and performed sacrifices.
False gods or deities that people worshiped instead of the true God.
Fortified cities and structures built to protect an area from enemy attacks.
A person who speaks on behalf of God and delivers his message to the people.
